title: They left home for Allah, and He gave them better.
subtitle: The emigrants who were wronged and then settled
then: Ibn Kathir says this may have been revealed about those persecuted so badly in Makkah that they {trap}left for Ethiopia to be able to worship their Lord{/trap}: Uthman bin Affan and Ruqayyah, Ja'far bin Abi Talib, Abu Salamah and others. {reward}Whoever gives up something for Allah, He compensates with something better.{/reward}
now: You turn down a job that would mean cutting corners. You move cities to protect your family's faith, leaving friends behind. It feels like pure loss. {reward}The verse says the account is not closed.{/reward}
old: What I give up for Allah is simply gone.
new: What I leave for Allah, He replaces with better, here and later.
try: Give up one small thing today purely for Allah's sake and trust Him with the gap.

title: Their two qualities: patience under harm, and trust in their Lord.
subtitle: What carried the emigrants through
then: This describes the emigrants of the verse before. Ibn Kathir says {idea}they bore their people's persecution with patience, putting their trust in Allah{/idea}, and {reward}He made their end good in this world and the Hereafter.{/reward}
now: The new country, the language you can't speak yet, the visa letter that has not come. You are tired of being strong. {idea}Patience is the holding on. Trust is knowing who holds you.{/idea}
old: I have to carry all of this by myself.
new: I hold on with patience and lean the weight on my Lord.
try: When the hard thing comes up today, say hasbiyallah and take one more patient step.

title: Every Messenger before was a man. Ask those who know.
subtitle: The objection that a Prophet cannot be human
then: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn Abbas that some Arabs said {trap}Allah is too great to send a human being as a Messenger.{/trap} This verse answers them: ask the people of the earlier Books {idea}whether their Prophets were humans or angels.{/idea}
now: You are unsure about something in your faith and you are tempted to guess or let it go. The verse gives a simple method: {idea}ask the people who know.{/idea} A teacher, a scholar, a trusted imam.
old: If I don't understand it, I can just decide for myself.
new: When I don't know, I ask those who have knowledge.
try: Write down one question about your faith and ask a knowledgeable person this week.

title: The Quran came to the Prophet ﷺ so he could explain it.
subtitle: Signs, Books, and a teacher who makes it clear
then: The earlier Messengers came with clear signs and Books. Ibn Kathir says the Quran was sent to the Prophet ﷺ {idea}so he could explain in detail what was mentioned in brief, and make clear what was not clear.{/idea} Then the goal: that people {reward}examine themselves and be guided.{/reward}
now: You hear a verse in the taraweeh prayer and it sounds beautiful, then it is gone. You never look up what it meant or how the Prophet ﷺ lived it. {idea}The explanation is there. Reflection is the part left to you.{/idea}
old: Listening to the Quran is enough.
new: The Quran comes with an explanation, and it is meant to make me think.
try: Pick one short verse today, read how the Prophet ﷺ explained or lived it, and think on it.

title: Do the plotters of evil feel so safe?
subtitle: Patience from Allah is not permission
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells us about {idea}His patience, and how He delays punishment{/idea} for those who plot evil and call others to it, even though He is able to bring it on them {trap}in a way they do not know where it comes from.{/trap}
now: You keep a small scheme going: the fake receipts, the lie you tell your spouse. Months pass and nothing happens. {trap}Quiet is not the same as safe.{/trap} {reward}The delay is time given to stop.{/reward}
old: Nothing bad has happened, so it must be fine.
new: Allah's delay is patience giving me time, not a sign I'm safe.
try: Name one thing you are getting away with and end it today.

title: He could take them in the middle of their busy day.
subtitle: No one escapes by being occupied
then: Ibn Kathir explains going to and fro as {trap}when they are busy with their daily business, travel, and other distracting activities.{/trap} He links it to the verse asking if towns felt safe from punishment at night while asleep, or by day while playing.
now: Calendar full, inbox at 300, three trips this month. You never get a quiet minute to think about where life is going. {trap}Being busy feels like protection.{/trap} {idea}It is not; it only fills the time you could have used to turn back.{/idea}
old: I'm too busy right now to think about my akhirah.
new: My busy days can end at any moment, so I make room for Allah inside them.
try: Put a five-minute reminder in your calendar today just to sit and remember Allah.

title: Or seize them through what they fear, yet He is Kind.
subtitle: The threat ends with mercy
then: Ibn Kathir says this can mean taking from them {trap}what they most fear{/trap}, which is even worse. Then the verse ends: your Lord is Kind and Merciful, {reward}because He does not hasten to punish.{/reward} He quotes the hadith that no one is more patient with hurtful words than Allah, who still gives them provision and health.
now: You have said and done things you are ashamed of, and still you woke up today with breath, food, and family. {reward}That is His patience with you.{/reward} The right response is to use it, not test it.
old: Since I'm still fine, Allah must not mind what I'm doing.
new: I'm still fine because my Lord is patient and merciful, and that is a chance to return.
try: Thank Allah today for one blessing you still have despite a sin you regret.

title: Even shadows lean to the right and left in prostration.
subtitle: Every created thing bows in its own way
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}everything that has a shadow leaning right and left, morning and evening, is prostrating to Allah by its shadow.{/idea} Mujahid said the prostration of the mountains is their shadows. Abu Ghalib Ash-Shaybani said the waves of the sea are its prayers.
now: Late afternoon, you walk past a lamppost and its shadow stretches long across the pavement. Your own shadow beside it. {idea}Both bowing without a word.{/idea} The question is whether your heart is bowing too.
new: Even my shadow submits to Allah; my heart can too.
try: Notice your shadow once today and use it as a reminder to make one sajdah.

title: Everything in heaven and earth bows, and the angels without pride.
subtitle: Creatures and angels all prostrate
then: After the shadows, the verse widens to all creatures. Ibn Kathir says {idea}the angels prostrate to Allah and are not too proud to worship Him.{/idea} This answers those described earlier in the surah whose hearts were too proud.
now: Your cat stretches, the birds wake at dawn, a whole city hums. {idea}All of it in quiet obedience.{/idea} You are the one creature who can choose to join in, or hold back out of pride.
old: Bowing down feels like losing my dignity.
new: Everything bows to Allah; joining them is where dignity lies.
try: In your next prayer, stay in sujood a few breaths longer than usual.

title: They fear their Lord above them and do as commanded.
subtitle: Angels who obey without delay
then: Ibn Kathir says the angels {idea}prostrate out of fear of their Lord{/idea}, and they continually obey Allah, doing what He tells them and avoiding what He forbids. Their awe is not anxiety; it shows up as obedience.
now: You say you fear Allah, but the fear only appears as guilt at night. You worry, then do nothing. {idea}The angels' fear turns straight into action.{/idea} One obeyed command is worth more than hours of worry.
old: Feeling guilty is the same as fearing Allah.
new: Real fear of Allah shows in doing what He asks.
try: Turn one worry about your deen into one action today.

title: Do not take two gods. He is One, so fear Him.
subtitle: One God, one source of fear
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells us {idea}there is no god but He, and no one else should be worshipped except Him{/idea}, for He is the Sovereign, Creator, and Lord of all things. The command is short: do not take two gods, fear Me alone.
now: You fear your manager, your in-laws, what people will say at the wedding, and also say you fear Allah. {trap}A heart with many masters is always tired.{/trap} {idea}Fear the One, and the rest get smaller.{/idea}
old: I have to keep everyone happy.
new: When I fear only Allah, other fears lose their grip.
try: Next time you fear someone's opinion, ask: what does Allah think of this?

title: Everything is His, and worship is His forever.
subtitle: So who else is there to fear
then: Ibn Kathir reports that wasiba, the word for worship being His, means forever, or obligatory, or purely for Him. {idea}Worship is due to Him alone from all in the heavens and on earth.{/idea} Then the verse asks: will you fear anyone other than Allah?
now: You lie awake fearing a layoff, a diagnosis, a phone call. {idea}Every one of those is in His hands.{/idea} {reward}The One who owns all of it is the One who loves you best.{/reward}
old: There are many powers in my life I need to fear.
new: Everything belongs to Allah, so He is the only one worth fearing.
try: Name your biggest fear tonight and hand it to Allah in a short dua.
